subject: Control-plane VLAN mapping & connector walkthrough for ACME private deployment

Subject: VLAN mapping for control-plane connectors - initial request

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the time this morning. We're trying to finalize the network handoff for our private VPC deployment (control-plane connectivity to Redwood private control endpoints). We have a couple of questions before the data center team begins the switch-level changes:

- Can you confirm the expected VLAN ranges for the control-plane peering vs management traffic?
- Are there any required L3 ACLs or port lists beyond 443 and 22 we should open to Redwood control-plane subnets?
- We prefer a single /24 per connectivity pair — does that match your recommended connector pattern?

I've attached our current draft diagram (vpc-vlan-draft.pdf). Sarah from Colab Partners is looping in on ops coordination.

Appreciate a short walkthrough or a simple mapping table we can hand to the NOC.

Thanks,
--
ACME Networks NOC
eng@acme-payments.com
(attachment: vpc-vlan-draft.pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VLAN mapping for control-plane connectors - initial request

Hi — thanks for the diagram, that's helpful. Quick answers up front, then a suggested mapping and a request to review during a short walkthrough: 

- VLAN ranges: we typically reserve 10.200.X.0/24 per connector pair (control-plane <-> customer management). For ACME I'd recommend 10.200.12.0/24 for control-plane peering; 10.200.13.0/24 for management/ops.
- Ports: primary egress is 443 (TLS) to our control-plane endpoints and 5222 for telemetry and health pings; SSH (22) is allowed only for scheduled support windows — don't open persistently. Additionally, we require UDP 1194 if you're using an IPsec/UDP encapsulation for the tunnel.
- Single /24 per pair: yes, that simplifies NOC routing tables.

Action: I'd like to run a 30-minute walkthrough with your NOC and our network lead (Jonas) to confirm ACLs, BGP neighbors (if applicable), and any MTU path MTU concerns. Proposed slots tomorrow: 09:00 or 14:00 PT. Please confirm.

Attaching a short annotated mapping (see vpc-vlan-draft.pdf — I'll follow up with a cleaned PDF after our sync).

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
(attachment referenced: vpc-vlan-draft.pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VLAN mapping for control-plane connectors - initial request

Thanks — a few technical clarifications from the runtime/connector side (summarized so your NOC can apply directly):

- IP addressing: we'll expect 10.200.12.1/24 on the Redwood side and 10.200.12.2/24 on ACME's side for the control-plane tunnel. Repeat pattern for management VLAN (10.200.13.1 / 10.200.13.2).
- BGP: optional. If you use BGP, we expect a private AS and an advertised /30 for the peering. If static, provision the two /24s and a default route to the tunnel endpoint.
- MTU/encapsulation: our recommended tunnel MTU is 1400 if you pass through encapsulating devices (VXLAN/IPsec). If you're doing direct L2 attach, keep MTU 1500 and test jumbo frames end-to-end.
- Required ports (egress): 443/TCP (control API), 5222/TCP (health/telemetry), 123/UDP (NTP) if you rely on NTP via the tunnel; NTP can be proxied but listing it avoids surprises.

I'll bring a one-page table to the walkthrough with exact ACL/CIDR examples.

Jonas
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

OLga / ACME — small ops checklist so the onboarding runbook team can prepare: 

- Can you confirm the maintenance window(s) you prefer for applying ACLs and L2 changes? We typically request a 2-hour window during off-peak.
- Audit evidence: ACME, please share your change ticket ID and point-of-contact for the NOC during the cut. We'll need the ticket to attach to our SOC2 evidence package.
- Monitoring hooks: we'll need a syslog endpoint and SNMPv3 read-only creds (or alternate telemetry) to integrate with our platform. Is that possible from the management VLAN?

Also — Kimberly, can you confirm that key rotation/access lists for SSH will be time-limited and that jump host egress is documented?

Marissa
Senior Program Manager, Deployments
marissa.cole@redwood.com
